Story: Hezekiah Shows His Treasures to Babylon
Retelling: After Hezekiah had been sick and recovered, Merodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to him, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick. Hezekiah was glad of the envoys, and showed them all the house of his precious things — the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious ointment, and all the house of his armour, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah did not show them. Then Isaiah the prophet came and asked, What said these men? and whence came they unto thee? and, What have they seen in thine house? Hezekiah answered that they had seen all that was in his house. Isaiah said, Hear the word of the LORD of hosts: Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon; nothing shall be left. And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah answered, Good is the word of the LORD which thou hast spoken — for, he thought, there shall be peace and truth in my days.
Discussion: Hezekiah showed Babylon everything, and the prophet showed him what that openness would cost. Reflect: 1) When does showing off what God gave become an invitation to lose it? 2) Why did Hezekiah accept a word of judgment so calmly — humility, or relief that it would not fall in his own days? 3) What are you displaying to powers that may one day come to collect?
Significance: A king's pride in his treasures opened the door to exile: what Hezekiah displayed to Babylon, Babylon would one day carry away.
